 US aviation authority grounds all departing flights, citing communication issues
 By Luke Cooper , Scout Wallen , Elissa Fitzgerald , Angela Lavoipierre and Brad Ryan in Washington DC Topic: Air Incidents
 Posted Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:12am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:12am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:12am Airplanes are grounded across the US. ( Reuters: Jonathan Ernst ) 
 Skip to timeline abc.net.au/news/follow-live-us-aviation-authority-grounds-all-flights/107385742 Link copied Share Share article All departing flights across the US have been grounded after a national halt order was issued by the nation's aviation regulator.
 The Federal Aviation Administration says a communication issue has affected all air route traffic control centres.
 Follow our live coverage.
 Submit a comment or question 
 Log in to comment Live updates
 Recap
 Here is a summary of key events so far:
 The US Federal Aviation Administration has issued a national ground stop for all departing flights   "due to extraordinary circumstance and reasons for safety" .
 The US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy confirmed the order was   given due to a communication issue affecting all air route traffic control centres .
 More than 5 ,000 flights have been cancelled across the US.
 The halt order is just the second ground stop issued by flight regulators since the September 11 terror attacks in 2001.

 Key Event
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 12:19pm Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 12:19pm US flights ground stop order about to be lifted: Reuters
 L By Luke Cooper
 We're seeing reports from Reuters that an update on today's ground stop order in the US is imminent.
 The news agency is citing a US official who says the halt order for departing flights across the country is about to be lifted.
 Reuters also says the US   Federal Aviation Administration is also reporting the cancellation of the earlier stop order.
 We're still waiting to hear from US   Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy at the White House.
 We'll provide you with further details as they come.
 React React Key Event
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 12:05pm Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 12:05pm What our readers on the ground are saying
 E By Elissa Fitzgerald
 I'm sitting in an airport lounge at DFW. The mood is hopeful, but nothing is moving
 - Jason 
 I'm on the Bay Area Rapid Transit BART train in San Francisco heading to SFO airport to get my flight tonight to Melbourne via Fiji. Looks like my flight is still On Time. All other Fiji Airway flights out of SFO appear delayed or cancelled!.Hopefully mine takes off on time so I don't miss my connection!
 - Paul 
 On a plane waiting to disembark at Chicago's OHare airport for 2 hours. We have been told they have run out of places to park planes.
 - Brendon 
 Aussie currently stuck at LAX, I was meant to fly to JFK at 12:36pm and our plane got grounded as it was on the runway about to take off. No real updates have been provided by American Airlines or LAX- my flight keeps getting moved. I am now meant to board at 7pm but this gets pushed back every hour
 - Ariella 
 Flights delayed here in Tokyo also
 - Jill Babicci 
 Thank you for sharing, everyone!
 We've got our fingers crossed for you that you won't be in for a long day (or night)!
 We will keep you updated with the latest information as it comes to hand, but also be on the lookout for information from your airlines and travel agents.
 React React Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 11:54am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 11:54am White House address expected shortly
 L By Luke Cooper
 We're seeing a note from the White House that US   Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy will soon speak to the media.
 We will keep you up to date with what is said at their press conference, as it comes to us.
 React React Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 11:49am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 11:49am 📷: Inside US airports and planes
 S By Scout Wallen
 The outage has now been underway for about four hours .
 Here is what it looks like at American airports and on planes.
 Robert Easton plays his harp after his flight was cancelled in Washington. (Reuters: Aaron Schwartz) Thousands of flights have been delayed or cancelled across the US. (AP: Mike Stewart) This traveller is waiting in the Dulles International Airport in Virginia. (Reuters: Daniel Heuer) Passengers on a plane after the ground stop order was issued. (Reuters: Angelina Katsanis) React React Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 11:41am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 11:41am Why are planes still taking off at some airports?
 E By Elissa Fitzgerald
 Flight Radar 24 shows plenty of planes in the sky over the US. And a good number of those are recent departures of passenger flights from US airports. It’s a funny-looking shutdown if, indeed, there still is one in place.
 - Dax 
 Flightradar App is showing flights in the US departing. I’ve just watched two planes depart JKF in the last 5 mins, one to Brussels, the other to London.
 - Brooke 
 I just watched Singapore Airlines flight SQ11 depart from LAX bound for Tokyo.
 - Russ 
 We've been getting plenty of comments about how international flights appear to still be on the move.
 It's true   — international departures have been running on a case-by-case consideration, so it's not surprising to see some still taking off.
 We've seen flights taking off on both the east and west coast, bound for Europe and Asia respectively.
 The US Federal Aviation Administration has not clarified which states are clear to permit departures, though.
 React React Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 11:35am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 11:35am ABC presenter's son stranded in New Orleans as plane ticket prices 'shoot up'
 N By Ned Hammond
 William McDonald told ABC Radio Brisbane he is three weeks into a trip across the US with a friend and is stuck at Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport .
 He says the price of flights has been shooting up.
 "My friend I think has just tried to buy tickets that are normally probably $US200 and now they’re up to like $US1,000," he says.
 William, the son of ABC radio presenter Bill McDonald , hopes the issue is something that can be resolved soon.
 "But then they said it could be seven hours, it could be 12 hours, it could be 24 hours," he says.
 "So very unhelpful time frame and I don’t really know what I’m working with here at the moment."
 He says the line at the information desk is "pretty extensive".
 "There's a few frustrated people … everyone's just sort of waiting to hear about what's going on, just any information, because apart from the seven to 24-hour time frame we've been given, that's all we have."
 React React Key Event
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 11:30am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 11:30am Trump hoses down suggestions of cyberattack
 E By Elissa Fitzgerald
 US President Donald Trump has just spoken with Fox News .
 He says it does not appear that the communications issue was caused by a cyberattack or AI.
 We'll let you know if he says more, as it comes to us.
 React React Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 11:28am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 11:28am Grounding planes was the right call, expert says
 S By Scout Wallen
   Shawn Pruchnik is anassociate professorat the aviation department at Ohio State University , a former pilot and an accident investigator . 
 Speaking to ABC News , he says the decision by the FFA to ground all planes was the right one. 
 "We have this significant problem of airplanes at higher altitudes that cannot communicate with air traffic control, so the solution to that is less airplanes up there," Pruchnik says.
 "Keep everyone down, let everyone land."
 Shawn Pruchnik says grounding all planes was the right call. (ABC News) He says it is too early to know what caused the communication issue.
 "Something broke maybe, a cyberattack, installing this new AI system that they're trying out, a software update … those are the types of the things at the top of the list that need to be investigated," Pruchnik says.
 "Some of those are more serious and difficult to fix."
 He says the planes still in the air will be able to land safely. 
 "We are trained as pilots to be able to approach an airport and land without radio communication … it is a little more high risk but there is less airplanes up there to worry about and we have collision protection in airplanes," he says.
 React React Key Event
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 11:21am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 11:21am Stranded Australian reports 'hundreds stuck in airport queues in New York'
 K By Kristy Sexton
 Trish Crabb is among the Australians caught up in the flight cancellations in the US .
 She said she and her husband were due to fly from JFK Airport in New York to Miami , when they learned their flight had been grounded.
 "The line-up is huge, at least 200 people in front of me and that's just for our Delta flight," Ms Crabb said.
 Queues inside New York City's JFK Airport. (Supplied: Trish Crabb) She said the couple, who are holidaying in the US, were due to fly to Miami, before travelling to Fort Lauderdale by car to board a cruise.
 "My husband is going to try and find us a hotel room somewhere close by, and hopefully we will be able to get a flight out at some stage," she said.
 Ms Crabb said everyone was "very calm" and most people were "taking it in their stride".
 React React Key Event
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 11:16am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 11:16am Any connection with yesterday's Microsoft outage?
 E By Elissa Fitzgerald
 Seems interesting timing with the Outlook outage yesterday. Any connection? 
 - Scott 
 Hi Scott,
 There's no apparent connection with yesterday's Microsoft outage .
 The Wall Street Journal is reporting that the communications outage affecting flights across the US appears to be linked to a network overseen by L3Harris Technologies .
 Microsoft has also said it has no indication that the ground stop is related to any of its services.
 React React Key Event
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 11:15am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 11:15am How nations neighbouring the US are handling the disruptions
 L By Luke Cooper
 The impacts from today's order to ground all departing flights across the US appears to be having varied impacts in Canada and Mexico .
 In the past two hours,   Nav Canada , the country's air service provider, confirmed that "traffic management measures" had been put in place in four locations to handle a jump in the number of flights heading there.
 In the past 10 minutes, the organisation has confirmed those measures have been lifted.
 "Our systems are operating normally. Travellers flying to or from the US should continue to check with their airline," Nav Canada said on X.
 Further south, Mexican authorities said earlier that American authorities had requested all flights there destined for the US remain grounded.
 The country's   Agencia Federal de Aviación Civil , the national civil aviation operator, has described the measure as "temporary", but says flights will not resume until aviation authorities in the US confirm it is safe to do so.
 React React Key Event
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 11:08am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 11:08am Advice for Australian travellers
 E By Elissa Fitzgerald
   Australians travelling to the US should expect to hear from their travel agents or airlines amid the ongoing ground stop, Australia's peak travel industry body says.
 "It is a developing situation, and there will be knock-on impacts for travellers," a statement from the Australian Travel Industry Association (ATIA) reads.
 Travellers at John F Kennedy International Airport in New York. (Reuters: Brendan McDermid) The body provided the following advice for travellers:
 If you're travelling in the next 72 hours and haven't yet been contacted by your travel agent, tour operator or airline, get in touch with them. Travellers due to depart soonest are the priority.
 If you're not travelling in the next 72 hours, please hold off contacting them for now, so agents, tour operators and airlines can prioritise the travellers who need support first.
 Check your airline's website or app for the latest   update on your flight.
 This is a developing situation, so keep an eye out for updates from your travel agent, tour operator and airline.
 React React Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 11:01am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 11:01am Stranded travellers make friends during the outage
 E By Emilie Gramenz in Washington DC
 In Washington's Ronald Reagan airport , Hadi Jeddy and Bob Priore have become fast friends.
 Hadi was heading to Chicago for a work trip, but with no idea when flights will be permitted to take off again, he made the quick decision to push the whole thing back.
 "We shifted everything by a week," he says.
 "This is abnormal. This is not what happens."
 Bob Priore (left) and Hadi Jeddy have become friends during the outage. (ABC News: Emilie Gramenz) Next to him was Bob, who was heading back to Buffalo after helping his son get settled in a new home in nearby McLean, Virginia .
 "I'm sitting next to Hadi, I said, 'Well, I've cancelled my flight, rebooked for tomorrow', and I said, 'Now I gotta find an Uber to McLean', and I looked at his shirt, and it said McLean, Virginia," Bob said.
 " Boy Scouts of America ," Hadi chimed in, gesturing at the emblem on his black fleece.
 "Well, that's where I'm going, so he offered me a ride back there," Bob said.
 "So we've made friends here, with an FAA outage."
 React React Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:58am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:58am What do pilots do when air traffic systems go down?
 L By Luke Cooper
 Aviation professor Skip Bailey has told The Associated Press that pilots and aircraft professionals are trained for situations exactly like this.
 Planes seen grounded and arriving at Chicago O'Hare International Airport. (Reuters: Jim Vondruska) The reason for this training is so they will be prepared if the radio on their plane malfunctions, he says.
 Bailey says no one expects air traffic controllers nationwide to lose the ability to communicate.
 In the event of a communication outage, pilots are expected to maintain the headings and vectors that controllers gave them before they lost contact.
 Then, if the outage continues, they revert to following their filed flight plan, according to Bailey.
 Pilots may also be able to communicate with each other over the radio even if they can't talk to controllers, and airliners have their own radar systems.
 "It's not mass chaos out there," Bailey said.
 "There's plenty of ways to try to communicate.
 "But not letting anybody take off again obviously is extremely important because we don’t want to put more aircraft into a system that’s already having an issue."
 React React Key Event
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:55am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:55am Senate commerce committee 'will be reviewing' tech issues, ranking member says
 E By Elissa Fitzgerald
 I mentioned earlier that the ranking member in the Senate's aviation subcommittee had called for a "thorough and complete investigation" into today's ground stop.
 Another senator has also flagged her intention to take up the matter.
 Senator Maria Cantwell, the ranking member for the commerce and transportation committee, says her team is in contact with the FAA.
 "Technology issues related to how planes communicate through primary frequencies, backup frequencies, and other issues will be something the commerce committee will be reviewing," she said.
 US Senator Maria Cantwell. (Reuters: Annabelle Gordon) React React Key Event
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:52am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:52am Flight cancellations top 3,300 within an hour
 L By Luke Cooper
 Less than an hour ago I reported that   FlightAware , an online aircraft-tracking website, was reporting that   about 10,500 flights   to and from the US had   already been delayed today.
 While I can now share with you that the number of delays has dropped slightly, there seems to be a rapid escalation in the number of flights being cancelled.
 In the past 45 minutes alone, cancellations have jumped from about 1,800 to more than 3,300 across the US, according to FlightAware.
 It's approaching 7pm local time in eastern US states and 4pm in western cities such as Los Angeles .
 Some major airlines are flagging that they are expect this disruption to persist for some time yet.
 React React Key Event
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:46am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:46am Australian woman stuck in San Diego
 S By Scout Wallen
 Australian woman   Rivkah-Louise Brown,   who is holidaying in the US, has been caught up in the aviation chaos.
 Rivkah was on a stop-over at San Diego International Airport,   on her way to Las Vegas to meet her fiancé, when her flight was cancelled. 
 Speaking to ABC News , she says she hasn't received any emails or communications from the airline.
 Rivkah-Louise Brown (right) had been on a Disney-themed cruise in the US. (Supplied: Rivkah-Louise Brown) "Passengers are just using their phones to find out what is happening," she says.
 "Everyone is being patient and relaxed which is nice."
 She says she's planning to stay in San Diego overnight and catch the bus to Las Vegas tomorrow.
 "Everyone is just trying to figure out a plan," she says.
 React React Key Event
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:43am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:43am Pacific-bound flights cleared for take-off: San Francisco Airport
 L By Luke Cooper
 A short time ago I reported that Alaska Airlines confirmed flights within the US state of Alaska and in Hawai’i "are not impacted" by the ongoing nationwide ground order.
 Minutes after that update from the carrier, San Francisco International Airport posted its own message online:
 Loading Twitter content The development suggests some planes might have been cleared for staggered take-offs if they are departing the continental US and flying over the Pacific Ocean .
 If we see any further information or an official confirmation of that, we will let you know here.
 React React Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:40am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:40am Eurocontrol suspends US-bound departures at FAA request
 E By Elissa Fitzgerald
 All US-bound traffic departing from Eurocontrol member states has been suspended at the FAA's request because of technical issues, Eurocontrol's website showed on Friday.
 There are 42 Eurocontrol member states, including the UK, France and Israel.
 Reporting with Reuters 
 React React Key Event
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:38am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:38am Ground stop outlasts 2023 incident
 E By Elissa Fitzgerald
 It has now been more than two hours since the ground stop was announced.
 That means today's situation has now continued for longer than the last US-wide ground stop.
 That one occurred in January 2023 and lasted 101 minutes , according to reporting at the time.
 The only other time US regulators ordered a nationwide ground stop was on September 11, 2001, following the terror attacks.
 Passengers at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport. (Reuters: David Ryder) React React Key Event
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:35am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:35am Flights within Alaska, Hawai'i 'not impacted'
 L By Luke Cooper
 In the past 20 minutes, Alaska Airlines has released a statement saying that while it is affected by the national ground order for departing flights, flights within the US states of Alaska and   Hawai'i "are not impacted".
 "Flights between the West Coast and Hawai’i can continue, and international flights from Honolulu have also been cleared for departure," a statement says.
 "Aircraft in the air are continuing to their destinations.
 "Because of the significance of the ground stop, we have cancelled some flights and diverted others."
 Meanwhile on mainland continental US, Delta Airlines has also issued its own statement.
 "No Delta flights are departing at this time and flights currently en route will continue to their destinations," the carrier said.
 "Customers should monitor their flight status on the Delta app or delta.com for the latest information."
 React React Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:32am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:32am US weather service now working
 S By Scout Wallen
 Earlier, we reported that the   US National Weather Service was experiencing   nationwide internet and communications problems. 
 That radar issue is now resolved, and the website is fully operational.
 Reporting with Reuters 
 React React Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:27am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:27am A deeper look into whether AI tool may have sparked nationwide flight disruption
 A By Angela Lavoipierre
 There are questions as to whether the recent nationwide rollout of a new AI air traffic tool known as " SMART"   could be behind the disruptions, so I’ve taken a closer look at it.
 The tool was rolled out on November 10 , several days ago, with no obvious issues – or at least none on this scale.
 Still, it’s worth mentioning that 25 Democrat members of Congress wrote a letter to the US Transport Secretary Sean Duffy last month, raising significant concerns about the rollout, including a lack of adequate testing and the risk of inaccuracies.
 “We are deeply concerned about the integration of any AI-enabled system into air traffic control systems, where decisions are literally a matter of life or death”, they wrote.
 A short time ago, the company behind the tool, Air Space Intelligence , posted on X , denying any link: "The current ground stop is not based on or a result of the SMART system, any product of ASI or our integration with FAA and ATC."
 React React Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:23am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:23am 📽️: Homeland Security Secretary says there is no safety threat
 S By Scout Wallen
 Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin addressed the media a short time ago.
 He says authorities   don't know yet   if a cyber attack is behind the incident , but has assured Americans that no one is in danger.   
 Loading... React React Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:20am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:20am Are flights still in the air?
 E By Elissa Fitzgerald
 Flight Radar 24 shows flights as normal!
 - Mark 
 Hi Mark,
 The national halt is only affecting planes still on the ground, with those already in the air allowed to complete their journeys.
 So, the longer the ground stop continues, the fewer planes we'll see in the air.
 The traffic outside Dulles International Airport in Virginia. (Reuters: Daniel Heuer) React React Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:12am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:12am Flights may be grounded, but Elon Musk has launched a rocket
 S By Scout Wallen
 While planes are grounded across the US, one take-off has been allowed to go ahead.
 A short time ago, SpaceX   launched its 15th Starship rocket flight from Texas on a mission to complete the first round-trip voyage, to orbit out and back to the very spot where it left Earth .
 It is carrying a batch of Starlink satellites, meaning it's a money-making endeavour for Elon Musk , as well as a high-stakes test for a rocket ship still under development.
 The 15th Starship launched from Texas. (AP: Eric Gay) React React Key Event
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:08am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:08am The latest from the FAA
 E By Elissa Fitzgerald
 The US Federal Aviation Administration says the nationwide ground stop remains in effect.  
 It adds that as enroute facilities recover, flights will be allowed to depart through coordination with the air traffic control system command centre.
 Reporting with Reuters 
 React React Key Event
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:06am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:06am How many flights have been delayed or cancelled?
 L By Luke Cooper
 Given this is an unfolding situation right across the United States , the numbers are still in flux.
 But, what we can tell you so far is that the nationwide ground halt order appears to be impacting tens of thousands of travellers in the US.
 FlightAware , an online aircraft tracking website, is reporting that around 10,500 flights into and out of the US have already been delayed today.
 The website also says that more than 1,800 flight services have been cancelled .
 As a reminder, it's just ticked past 6pm local time in the US's eastern states and 3pm in western cities such as Los Angeles .
 Some major airlines have also flagged they are expecting this disruption to persist for some time yet.
 React React Key Event
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:59am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:59am Radars and radio frequencies also affected: CNN
 S By Scout Wallen
 CNN is reporting the nationwide flights disruption is also affecting   air traffic control radars and radio frequencies .
 CNN says it spoke to a source familiar with what controllers are dealing with, who told them that controllers do not have any clarity on the cause and what exactly is going on.
 The   US National Weather Service is also currently experiencing   nationwide internet and communications problems. 
 This could be preventing people from accessing services on its website.
 There is no evidence that the incidents are linked.   
 React React Key Event
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:57am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:57am Is the US flight disruption linked to Microsoft outage or AI tool rollout?
 A By Angela Lavoipierre
 Speculation is rife on social media about a possible connection between the 21-hour Microsoft outage, which was resolved this morning, and the US flight disruptions.
 However, US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters: "I don’t see any reason to connect those two at all." 
 Separately, he was asked about reports that the FAA was due to roll out its new artificial intelligence-based air traffic tool today, and whether that could be the reason for the comms outage.
 He said: "We’re looking at that."
 React React Key Event
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:54am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:54am Telco responsible for FAA's tech systems 'not aware of issue'
 E By Elissa Fitzgerald
 US telco Verizon says its network is "fully functioning", and   it is not aware of any issue related to air traffic control systems.   
 The US Federal Aviation Administration awarded Verizon a 15-year contract potentially worth $US2.4 billion ($3.5 billion) to upgrade the agency's technology systems.
 FAA technicians are currently investigating the cause of the communications failure.
 React React Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:46am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:46am 📽️: Footage shows grounded flights in LA
 S By Scout Wallen
 The   Los Angeles International Airport would normally be a hub of activity on a Friday afternoon, but this footage shows a quieter scenario.
 Loading... React React Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:43am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:43am 'I will be demanding answers,' US senator says
 E By Elissa Fitzgerald
 US Senator Tammy Duckworth, the ranking member in the Senate's aviation subcommittee, has called for a "thorough and complete" investigation into the ground stop.
 "Whatever led to the nationwide ground stop will warrant a thorough and complete investigation," she wrote on X.
 "As Aviation Subcommittee Ranking Member, I'll be demanding answers from the FAA."
 Loading Twitter content React React Key Event
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:39am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:39am 📷: What it's like inside US airports right now
 S By Scout Wallen
 This flight shutdown began on Friday afternoon , local time, when many Americans would have been commuting for the weekend.
 A reminder that there has been no update as to when the order will be lifted. 
 Here's what it looks like inside some US airports right now.
 People stand in line at John F. Kennedy International Airport in New York. (Reuters: Angelina Katsanis) Commuters are waiting in airports aross the country. (Getty Images via AFP: Finn Gomez) Flights are being delayed across the country. (AP: Ethan Swope) React React Key Event
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:38am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:38am How long the US's biggest airlines expect disruption to last
 E By Elissa Fitzgerald
 American Airlines has told customers disruptions are likely "for the rest of the day", depending on the duration of the nationwide grounding.
 "It will be all hands on deck across American to get customers on their way as soon as possible when the FAA lifts this ground stop," a statement reads.
 It is just past 5.30pm in New York and 2.30pm in Los Angeles.   
 Loading Twitter content Another of the country's largest carriers, United Airlines , has also issued its own statement addressing the disruptions.
 "United flights that are already airborne will continue," the company says.
 "New domestic flights will not depart while the FAA ground stop remains in place.
 "United will work with our customers to get them to their destinations once this issue is resolved."
 React React Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:30am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:30am Flights can land safely, says Mullin
 B By Brad Ryan in Washington DC
   Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin   says not all communications are down, and he has stressed that flights in the air right now would be able to land safely.
 "We are able to communicate at certain levels, but it's overwhelmed some of the systems we have," he said.
 " We're assured that everybody is safe.
 "Everybody that's going to be in the air, that's currently on a plane, your loved ones, as I said, we're going to get you on the ground, and we're doing it in a safe manner."
 US Homeland Security Secretary Markmwayne Mullin. (Reuters: Elizabeth Frantz) React React Key Event
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:29am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:29am The latest from the FAA
 E By Elissa Fitzgerald
   The   US Federal Aviation Administration says flights have been grounded due to a temporary telecommunications outage.   
 "Out of an abundance of caution all flights have been halted," the agency said in a statement.
 "Every flight has been accounted for and international flights will be handled on a case-by-case basis."
 Loading Twitter content React React Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:27am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:27am Flight Radar shows busy airspace
 S By Scout Wallen
 To give you an idea of just how busy the US's airspace is right now, here is a shot of the country from the FlightRadar24 website.
 The aircraft monitor shows hundreds of flights are still in the air over the country.
 As we've mentioned, the national halt order does not prevent those flights from landing, it will only impact planes still on the ground.
 Flight Radar shows the US airspace is busy. (Supplied: Flight Radar) React React Key Event
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:19am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:19am 'This isn't another 9/11,' Homeland Security Secretary says
 B By Brad Ryan in Washington DC
 US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin has briefed reporters at the White House on the national ground stop.
 He said there was no threat to the public, but the root cause of the problem is not known.
 US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin. (Reuters: Elizabeth Frantz) "There's no reason for the public to be afraid or scared for your loved ones," he said.
 "This isn't another 9/11.
 "This is a telecommunications outage. This is much different."
 Mullin could not say how long it would take for things to return to normal.
 "This isn't just going to be resolved and turned around within the hour," he said.
 He would not rule out a cyber attack, nor problems related to new AI-powered technology being rolled out in air control towers.
 US media is reporting that FBI and law enforcement sources do not believe the problem is the result of a cyber attack.
 Mr Mullin said there was also no reason to think yesterday's global Microsoft outage was linked to the issue.
 React React Key Event
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:14am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:14am What we know so far
 L By Luke Cooper
 The nationwide ground stop came after the FAA first halted traffic in Chicago due to air traffic control issues.
 The following order then stopped   "all departing traffic … until further notice". 
 The regulator says all international flights will be managed on a case-by-case basis.
 The order means flights already in the air may land but flights on the ground cannot take off.
 This is only the second nationwide ground stop in the United States since the September 11 terror attacks .
 The last one was in January 2023 , when domestic departures were paused for less than two hours.
 React React Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:08am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:08am Flights grounded across the US
 L By Luke Cooper
 Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of the unfolding flight halt affecting all aircraft currently operating in the United States .
 The US Federal Aviation Administration has issued a national ground stop "due to extraordinary circumstance and reasons for safety". 
 It comes after the agency earlier reported serious air traffic control communications issues.
 My ABC colleagues and I will keep you up to date here with ongoing developments and information as it becomes available to us.
